VTSearch · experiment report · 2026-07-13

Structural search comes home — screenshots & scanned documents

VLAD-of-SIFT barely retrieved logos in the wild. On flat rasters — no perspective, no rotation — we ask three questions: is the domain the problem, is a 3-DoF fit the right geometry, and does SuperPoint+LightGlue earn the backend slot the design doc reserves?

VTSearch screenshot-iconography study · HLTCOE grid · sequel to the 2026-07-11 OpenLogo structural-search report
13,321doc pages + screenshots
463seeded queries, 4 corpora
1.6Mimage pairs matched
3.3Mgeometric fits (3- & 4-DoF)

TL;DR. ① Flat rasters alone don't fix the production pipeline — SIFT itself was a bottleneck all along: only 5.1% of true scanned-document pairs verify under SIFT, because rubber stamps and letterhead emblems are line art, which SIFT can barely anchor. ② Swap the feature backend and the story flips: SuperPoint+LightGlue verifies 41% of the same true pairs (7× SIFT) and, used as the ranker, reaches AP 0.395 / 0.481 on the two document corpora — double SigLIP (0.204 / 0.235), the first configuration in either study where structural search beats the deep embedder on a real corpus. ③ Below ~128 px none of this matters: small flat icons are feature-starved for every backend — the true-pair verify rate collapses from 43% (≥256 px) to ≤5% (128–256 px) to ≈1% below that. The screenshot-iconography subgenre lives almost entirely under that cliff. ④ The 3-DoF fit (x, y, scale — no rotation) is a free precision win: AP identical to 4-DoF, but false verifications drop sharply (synth SIFT verified-precision 0.77 → 0.98). ⑤ LightGlue's denser matches over-fire the SIFT-calibrated cold gate — it needs its own inlier floor (≈24, not 8). ⑥ On the synthetic benchmark, querying with the canonical logo artwork beats an in-context crop 2.2×. Upscaling tiny query crops does nothing. ⑦ (tiling extension) Most of the small-icon failure was the big canvas, not the small target: matching against 224 px sliding-window tiles instead of whole screenshots lifts SIFT's true-pair verify rate from 0.2% to 14% (32–64 px) and from 3.8% to 20% (64–128 px) at unchanged false-positive rate, and max-over-tiles VLAD multiplies Stage-1 AP 5.4× — the absolute size floor only survives below ~32 px.

SETUPFour flat-raster corpora, one production pipeline

The OpenLogo study ended on a suspicion: maybe "in the wild" — perspective, curvature, clutter — is what breaks structural search, and VTSearch's real deployment targets (screenshots, scanned documents) would be kinder. Those images have no perspective at all: a repeated logo, stamp, or icon differs from its template by translation and scale only — 3 degrees of freedom. This study tests that hypothesis on four corpora, and uses it to answer two roadmap questions: does a 3-DoF geometric model beat the production 4-DoF similarity fit, and does the SuperPoint+LightGlue backend the design doc reserves (the "LightGlue v2 slot") earn its integration?

  • SPODS — 1,062 scanned document pages, 64 logo/stamp classes (~30 pages each), ground-truth boxes. Median mark ≈ 1.3% of the page.
  • StaVer — 259 scanned pages, 36 multi-instance stamp classes (+171 singleton distractors). Its boxes are a fixed 699×309 window, so query crops carry some letterhead context (see caveats).
  • Rico — 9,000 Android UI screenshots, the 26 most frequent annotated icon classes (menu, back-arrow, search, …). Class-level ground truth: two "search" icons in different apps count as the same class even when the artwork differs.
  • Synth — 3,000 Rico screenshots with 48 simple-icons brand logos pasted at exact known (x, y, scale), 18–220 px, 30 placements each: instance ground truth by construction, plus a clean 192 px canonical render of every logo for canonical-artwork queries.

Pipelines mirror production exactly as in the prior study (same vtscore code paths, VLAD codebook, thresholds, cold-start gate). New: every query–candidate pair is matched once per backend (SIFT+Lowe, or SuperPoint+LightGlue at 2,048 keypoints / long side 1,536) and both geometries are fit on identical correspondences, so backend and geometry are cleanly isolated variables. On the two document corpora (≤1,062 pages) we also run each backend exhaustively over the whole corpus ("direct" rows) — the no-Stage-1 ceiling. 463 queries, 1.6M matched pairs, 3.3M RANSAC fits.

EXPERIMENT ADoes structural search work better on flat rasters?

Setup. The production example flow: crop one ground-truth instance (or drop in the canonical artwork), search, measure ranking quality against every other instance in the corpus. Metrics over the full corpus per query; mean AP shown, medians and P@10/R@50 in the data file.

Documents: yes — but only after swapping the backend. The production two-stage pipeline improves over its OpenLogo showing (AP 0.075 on SPODS, 0.176 on StaVer, vs 0.031 in the wild) yet stays far below SigLIP — its Stage-1 recall is still the wall (R@50 0.066 on SPODS). The same corpora under SuperPoint+LightGlue direct matching: AP 0.395 and 0.481, P@10 0.502 — 3× direct SIFT and 2× SigLIP. For corpora of this size (≈1k images) exhaustive LightGlue matching is ~86 pairs/s on one A100, i.e. ~12 s per query: viable as an on-demand "deep search" today.

The hybrid is the deployable version of that result. SigLIP retrieval with SP+LG 3-DoF verification of the top-50 hits AP 0.479 on StaVer — statistically the same as the 0.481 exhaustive ceiling at 1/20th the matching cost — and 0.242 on SPODS (the gap to 0.395 is SigLIP recall: R@50 0.246; verification cannot add recall, exactly as the OpenLogo study concluded).

Screenshots: the task splits in two. On Rico, every pipeline lands at AP ≈ 0.11 — but that number means something different: Rico's ground truth is semantic (all "menu" icons count), while structural search retrieves instances. Direct SIFT's P@10 of 0.335 with 81% verified-precision shows it doing its actual job: finding pixel-identical repeats of the same artwork (same app, same system icon set) and being right about them. Finding all conceptual matches is the deep-embedder detector's job, not geometry's. On Synth — true instance ground truth — absolute numbers are low for everyone (best: direct SIFT 3-DoF 0.111) for a reason the size analysis below makes exact: most pasted logos sit below the feature-size floor, and flat-color brand glyphs are the most feature-starved imagery in either study.

EXPERIMENT B3-DoF (x, y, scale) vs the production 4-DoF fit

Setup. Same correspondences, two RANSAC fits: the production 4-DoF similarity (cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D) and a custom 3-DoF scale+translation estimator (2-point minimal samples, exhaustively enumerated when C(n,2) ≤ 2000 — deterministic and slightly stronger than sampled RANSAC; production thresholds and sanity gates unchanged). If screenshots and scans truly never rotate, removing the rotation DoF should cost nothing and deny RANSAC one axis of freedom to hallucinate with.

Finding: ranking is indifferent, precision is not. ΔAP between the fits is within noise on every corpus × backend (largest: +0.02 for SP+LG on StaVer). But the false-positive side moves consistently in 3-DoF's favor — synth SIFT verified-precision 0.77 → 0.98, SPODS SIFT 0.45 → 0.64, and SP+LG's per-query false verifies drop ~7% — with true-pair rates essentially unchanged. This is the OpenLogo Experiment B result run in reverse: there, adding DoF (4→6→8) bought nothing but false verifications; here, removing one sheds them for free, because on axis-aligned rasters the rotation axis only ever fits noise. The green "found it here" box the user sees also gets cleaner. Recommendation: make 3-DoF the default fit for screenshot/document image media (a per-media-profile choice, mirroring how the design doc already scopes geometry per media type).

EXPERIMENT CSuperPoint+LightGlue vs SIFT as the matching backend

Setup. The design doc reserves a learned-feature slot behind the StructuralMatcher protocol ("SuperPoint + LightGlue v2" — no public LightGlue v2 exists; we use the official cvg/LightGlue, current head, SuperPoint weights). We built that backend (vtscore/media/structural_splg.py on branch claude/splg-structural-backend, StructuralMatcher-conformant, smoke- and unit-tested) and ran it through the identical harness.

On documents, the backend is transformational. 41% of true SPODS pairs verify under SP+LG vs 5.1% under SIFT (20 vs 3.1 mean inliers on true pairs). The prior study located 65% of failures at the descriptor-matching step — for line art, SuperPoint+LightGlue simply fixes that step, and the direct-search AP triples.

It over-fires the SIFT-calibrated gate. At the production floor (8 inliers ⇒ v=0.5) SP+LG's false-pair rate is 5.7% vs SIFT's 0.14% — on a 1,000-page corpus that's dozens of spurious "verified" badges per query (73/query observed). The sweep above is the calibration curve; ship the SP+LG backend with its own floor (≈24), or let the trained verification classifier absorb it once votes exist (the prior study showed those labels are precisely calibration).

On small screenshot icons, SP+LG does not rescue anything — SIFT is actually the better of the two. Rico true pairs: 0.7% (SIFT) vs 0.3% (SP+LG); synth below 64 px both ≈1%. Mechanism: SuperPoint's keypoint budget spreads over the whole screenshot and leaves a 30 px glyph 0–3 detections, which LightGlue's confidence filter then discards; SIFT's scale-space at least fires on the glyph's corners. The cliff is a resolution and texture floor, not a matcher deficiency — no correspondence backend fixes a target with three corners.

TARGETSWhich marks succeed, which fail

Per-class means under the strongest structural pipeline per corpus, best and worst. The pattern repeats across corpora: structure-rich, multi-element marks succeed (emblems with internal detail, ornamental stamps, the Rust gear); solid silhouettes, thin-line glyphs, and anything under ~64 px fail — including a 164 px GitHub octocat whose 70 SIFT keypoints all sit on one featureless contour. Text-only stamps fail structurally but are exactly where SigLIP shines (stamp_12: SigLIP 0.67), previewing the hybrid's complementarity.

SYNTHCanonical artwork vs crops, and the scale cliff

Three synth-specific results. (1) Canonical queries win: AP 0.173 vs 0.079 for crops — the clean render has every feature the artwork owns, a crop only the ones that survived compositing. The UI should invite "upload the logo itself", not only region-crops. (2) The scale cliff has exact coordinates here (placements are log-uniform 18–220 px with known size): verification only starts to function at 64–128 px and reaches merely 10% (SP+LG) / 7% (SIFT) at 128–256 px — flat-color brand glyphs are hard even when large. (3) Upscaling tiny query crops 2× before feature extraction changes nothing (AP ±0.002 across 60 tiny-query cases, both backends): interpolation manufactures pixels, not structure. The missing information simply is not in a 24 px raster.

When SIFT-3-DoF does verify a pasted logo it is almost never wrong (verified-precision 0.98): on screenshots the structural verifier is a high-precision, low-recall instrument — a "confirm" button, not a "find" button.

TILINGSmall target, or big canvas? Subdivide and see

Setup. The size cliff has two candidate causes: the target is too small to carry features (absolute floor), or the target is fine and the canvas drowns it — the per-image keypoint budget (1,024 SIFT / 2,048 SuperPoint) is allocated by detection score across the whole screenshot, and LightGlue must match a ~10-keypoint query against a 2,048-keypoint scene. To separate them we re-ran the verification pair study with the candidate side cut into 224 px tiles at 50% overlap (mean 125 tiles/screenshot; any target ≤ 112 px is fully inside some tile), scored as best-over-tiles, in two variants: tiles at native resolution (removes dilution) and tiles upscaled 2× (additionally feeds SuperPoint's fixed receptive field more pixels — SIFT already octave-doubles internally). Same queries, same pairs, same gates. Tiling multiplies the false-fire opportunities ~125×, so alongside the production gate we report each condition at a gate-matched operating point (smallest inlier floor with pair-FPR ≤ 1%).

Finding: it was mostly the canvas. On identical pairs, tiling lifts SIFT's true-pair verify rate from 0.2% → 14% (32–64 px), 3.8% → 20% (64–128 px), and 7.5% → 18% (128–256 px) — 5–70× — at essentially unchanged FPR, and the pattern replicates on real Rico icons (0.1% → 3.9% and 0.4% → 7.7% in the same buckets). Dilution of the keypoint budget, not absolute target size, was the dominant failure mode above ~32 px. The 2× tiles add meaningfully only in the smallest buckets (SIFT <32 px: 4.1% → 7.9%), confirming a residual resolution effect exactly where pixels run out.

SP+LG under tiling needs its gate more than ever. Raw tiled SP+LG posts eye-watering numbers (33–55% TPR in every bucket) — and a 33% false-pair rate that makes them meaningless. At the matched gate (floor 24) the genuine improvement survives only for targets ≥ 64 px (128–256 px: 10.4% → 28%, ~3× whole-image); below 64 px its true matches produce inlier counts indistinguishable from its hallucinations, and gate-matched tiled SIFT beats it (14% vs 1–7% at 32–64 px). For small flat iconography, the classic detector inside a small window is the more trustworthy instrument.

The absolute floor is real but narrow. Below ~32 px — where even zero-dilution query crops yield 0–3 keypoints — tiling recovers only 4–8% (SIFT @2x). That band, and only that band, still needs a non-correspondence method.

What this says about the roadmap

The flat-raster hypothesis was half right: geometry was never the obstacle (3-DoF ≈ 4-DoF everywhere), features were. Where targets are big enough to carry structure — scanned documents — the reserved SuperPoint+LightGlue slot pays for itself immediately; where they aren't — small screenshot iconography — no correspondence matcher will, and the subgenre needs a different instrument.

1 — Integrate the SP+LG backend for document-like media. The code is ready on branch claude/splg-structural-backend (StructuralMatcher-conformant; needs an fp16 descriptor path in StructuralFeatures.compact() and an install extra for lightglue+kornia). Ship it with its own cold-gate floor (≈24 inliers) and 3-DoF as the default fit for screenshot/document media profiles. Expected effect, measured: 2× SigLIP AP on document corpora, verified-region overlays on half of all true pairs.

2 — The deployable search config today is hybrid. SigLIP retrieval + SP+LG 3-DoF verification hit the exhaustive-matching ceiling on StaVer at 1/20th the cost. For corpora ≤ ~5k images, offer direct SP+LG matching as an explicit "deep structural search" (≈12 s/query on one A100).

3 — Small-icon search: tile it. The tiling extension showed the sub-128 px failure was mostly canvas dilution, and both fixes fit the existing architecture: tile-VLAD Stage-1 (per-tile VLAD vectors, max-over-tiles cosine — multi-vector medias on the existing codebook) and tiled Stage-2 verification with SIFT (best-over-tiles MatchStats; FPR stays production-safe without recalibration). Only the <32 px band still needs a non-correspondence method (multi-scale normalized cross-correlation — a cheap, exact 3-DoF template sweep on flat rasters).

4 — Stage-1 remains the production wall — unchanged conclusion from OpenLogo, now measured on four more corpora: VLAD R@50 ≤ 0.07 on three of four. Every structural gain in this report routes around Stage 1 (hybrid or direct); nothing rescues it from within.

Method & caveats

Fidelity. SIFT extraction, VLAD aggregation, Lowe matching, 4-DoF RANSAC settings, MatchStats, cold gate, thresholds, and rerank ordering call or mirror production vtscore line-for-line (SIFT-parity smoke test: identical inlier counts). The 3-DoF estimator and SP+LG backend are the exact modules proposed for integration. Matching runs once per (query, candidate, backend); both geometries fit shared correspondences. SP+LG extraction: 2,048 keypoints, long side 1,536 — deliberately the learned backend's best practical config (SIFT keeps its production 1,024 cap; noted as a budget asymmetry in the backend's favor).

Caveats. (1) StaVer's ground-truth boxes are a fixed window, so its query crops include letterhead context — this inflates cross-page text matching and is part of why LightGlue's false-verify rate is highest there; SPODS (tight boxes) is the cleaner document read. (2) Rico ground truth is semantic-class level; its AP numbers measure a concept task that structural search is not built for — the per-query verified-precision numbers are the instance-level signal. (3) Synth logos are monochrome simple-icons renders: the hardest, least-textured end of real iconography; treat its absolute APs as a lower bound. (4) No voting simulation this time — the prior study established labels ≈ calibration on the structural path. (5) "LightGlue v2" does not exist publicly; results use official cvg/LightGlue (SuperPoint weights, current head). (6) Cold start only, single seeds; corpus sizes 259–9,000.

Artifacts. Everything under /exp/sgreenberg/experiments/screenshot-search/: corpora (webdataset shards + corpus.jsonl), 463 query crops + features, pair manifests, 1.6M matched correspondences, per-query JSON, results/report_data.json, and the runnable pipeline (pipeline.sh, extract_*.py, match_*.py, score_pairs.py, aggregate.py). Integration code: vtscore/media/structural_geometry.py + structural_splg.py + tests on branch claude/splg-structural-backend.
